(2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the English gloss so the sentence set beside the Hebrew header is the header's own rendering in the folded verse, and any following sentence retained is labelled as the oracle's first line rather than as the header. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the re-spliced run must return byte tier against its cited ref (the test that killed the original), and the quote/gloss pair must satisfy parity -- the English offered for a Hebrew form must be that form's rendering in the folded verse, carried in curly quotes with an inline web: ref in the same field.

P05-002.challenge_claim: OL (medium): both pointed runs are labelled byte tier but re-collate only at NFD, and the row's own opening scene-turn run recurs BYTE-IDENTICALLY one verse past its closing seam with no disclosure, so the strongest byte-true rival goes unnamed. P05-002.grounds: TIER LIMB UPHELD, held in common: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא at oshb:Isa.17.4 and נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at oshb:Isa.17.6 each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY while both are self-labelled byte tier -- the same degraded-quote class as the neighbouring header row. The substance behind them survives: the signature is verse-final at oshb:Isa.17.6 in the bytes (tokens 15-18) and its title stack genuinely differs from נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת closing oshb:Isa.17.3, so this is a second distinct bracket and not a repeated formula. BOTH CROSS-SEAM LIMBS NAME REAL UNDISCLOSED SIGNALS, one per seam, and both need their tier corrected. OL's back-seam FACT re-derives exactly: the two-word run בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא inside the row's own opening formula at oshb:Isa.17.4 is byte-identical, accent for accent, to the verse-initial run at oshb:Isa.17.7 one verse past this row's close. But the INFERENCE is mechanically backwards: the row treats that run as an ONSET marker, so a byte-identical verse-initial recurrence at Isa.17.7 marks the NEXT unit's onset and corroborates this row's close rather than arguing continuity into it. The genuine rival it raises is series-level, and neither lens reached it: the run recurs a THIRD time verse-initial at oshb:Isa.17.9, where it is byte-DISTINCT from the other two and matches them only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier. So what goes undisclosed is a three-site chapter series of which only two sites are byte-identical, and the live rival is one composite unit with internal stanzas. LF's front-seam hook is real but its tier is unstated and cannot be byte: the two tokens are כִּכְב֤וֹד at oshb:Isa.17.3 and כְּב֣וֹד at oshb:Isa.17.4 (each byte tier at its own ref), which are neither byte-equal NOR skeleton-equal -- a prefixed comparative form against the bare construct -- so the hook is lexeme-level only. LF's high severity overstates: the row's seam is independently carried by a verse-final signature with its own distinct title stack, and both cited marks verify at tier-3, single witness, correctly typed and correctly oriented (segs after Isa.17.3 and after Isa.17.6).
P05-002.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (3) device_notes: disclose the verse-initial recurrence at Isa.17.7 explicitly and state what it argues (a fresh onset past this row's close, corroborating the cut) so the cross-seam device is on the record either way; and add the lexeme-level 'glory' hook across Isa.17.3|Isa.17.4 with its tier named as lexeme/root and explicitly NOT as byte or skeleton identity of the two tokens. P05-003.grounds: TIER LIMB UPHELD: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא and קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.17.7 and בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא at oshb:Isa.17.9 each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY while all three are self-labelled byte tier, so the row carries no quotation-grade pointed evidence at all. LF'S LIMB UPHELD EXACTLY: the rejected alternative places the finer-cut rival at 'the row's fourth verse' while the row's own rationale names oshb:Isa.17.9, which is the THIRD verse of the Isa.17.7-Isa.17.11 span -- a positional reference standing where a verse anchor belongs, and wrong by one. VERIFIED AND OWING NOTHING: the divine title at oshb:Isa.17.7 is genuine and is the only title verse between Isa.12.6 and Isa.29.19 (25 title verses book-wide, title-construct object, unit = verses); both cited marks verify at tier-3, single witness, correctly typed as setumah and correctly oriented, the segs standing after Isa.17.6 and after Isa.17.11 and so bracketing this span; one paseq seg is inventoried at Isa.17.9, count-only and single witness, and the row makes no claim depending on it.

P05-005.grounds: ADDRESSEE LIMB UPHELD. The row's own quoted frame כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י at oshb:Isa.18.4 ends in the dative אֵלַ֔י, which names the prophet as the recipient of that speech, so 'without a fresh addressee shift' is contradicted by the very bytes the row cites. Two address turns stand immediately before it: the imperative address לְכ֣וּ מַלְאָכִ֣ים קַלִּ֗ים at oshb:Isa.18.2 and the universal vocative כָּל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵ֖ל וְשֹׁ֣כְנֵי אָ֑רֶץ opening oshb:Isa.18.3 and closing on the second-person plural תִּשְׁמָֽעוּ (all byte tier). The frame is correctly owned as the divine one rather than the royal-messenger class -- that verse is a divine-frame site by inventory, and the royal-messenger sites are confined to the narrative zone. MARK LIMB REFUTED, on the challenge's own convention. The seg inventoried at Isa.18.3 stands AFTER that verse's words, so it marks Isa.18.3|Isa.18.4 -- precisely the divine-speech onset that this row's rejected alternative DOES weigh -- and not the vocative. Nothing corroborates a cut at the vocative: the inventory records no seg after Isa.18.2, this span's marks standing at Isa.17.14 and Isa.18.3 and Isa.18.7. Read with the after-the-verse orientation these packets apply elsewhere, the tier-3 layer SUPPORTS the rival the row already names instead of exposing one it missed, and it remains weak, single witness and non-driving in either direction. DEGRADED-RUN LIMB UPHELD, band corrected. ה֥וֹי אֶ֖רֶץ צִלְצַ֣ל כְּנָפָ֑יִם at oshb:Isa.18.1 and both כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י and אשקוטה אֶשְׁקֳטָ֖ה at oshb:Isa.18.4 each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY while all three are self-labelled byte tier. The escalation to high rests on the variant-note pair carrying the strictest fidelity standard; that is a register argument rather than a distinct defect class, and the degradation in fact lives in the pointed read-form, since the written form is unpointed in the extract and is a bare-consonant form mention. The row's variant-note engagement is otherwise a real strength that should survive revision: the doubled pair does sit in the letter bytes of oshb:Isa.18.4, the row names which form is unpointed and which is pointed, the note inventory carries exactly one note there, and it is the only variant-note verse anywhere in oshb:Isa.16.13-Isa.19.15 (49 such verses book-wide, unit = verses). (2) boundary_rationale: strike 'without a fresh addressee shift' and put the byte-supported reading in its place -- the frame is explicitly addressed to the prophet by the dative standing inside the row's own quote, and it follows an imperative address and a universal vocative -- then re-argue the hold-as-one-unit decision on the ground that survives: the woe cry bounds the unit and the next unit opens at the following oracle header. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: keep the divine-speech-onset rival and add that the tier-3 seg standing after Isa.18.3 corroborates exactly that rival while remaining non-driving; do NOT add a vocative rival, since nothing in the marks layer points there. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: each re-spliced run returns byte tier against its cited ref; no no-shift or continuity claim may survive that the row's own quoted bytes contradict; and every parashah citation must resolve to the after-the-verse orientation and validate against the inventory under the claimed type at the MT key, single witness.

P05-008.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, object first. The scene-turn formula spliced from MT 19:16's own bytes is “בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא” (skeleton “ביום ההוא”); swept over the staged Masoretic text it stands in SIX verses of the row's own span — MT 19:16, 19:18, 19:19, 19:21, 19:23, 19:24 — against the row's ‘recurs four further times through the row's own span (sweep: 5 sites)’. Five of the six are verse-initial; MT 19:21 carries it mid-verse (skeleton index 38, after “and the Egyptians will know Yahweh”). So the digit is recoverable only under a verse-initial restriction the row never states: the OBJECT is under-specified, not merely the number, and the count also names no unit where campaign practice requires verses or occurrences. TIER CORRECTION to the LF item: the six sites are NOT byte-identical. At byte tier the formula as spelled at MT 19:16 stands in only four verses of chs 19-24 (MT 19:16, 22:8, 23:15, 24:21) and in only ONE verse of ch 19; all six match at accent_stripped and at skeleton. OL's skeleton label is the correct tier and LF's ‘byte-identical’ is a false tier claim inside a challenge. P05-009.challenge_claim: The 'no internal tier-1 seam' warrant is argued past its strongest counterevidence — a verse-initial divine-speech onset at MT 20:3 coinciding with the row's only in-span parashah mark — the frame at MT 20:2 is mislabelled as interpretive when it introduces the command, and both pointed runs labelled byte tier re-collate at NFD only.
P05-009.grounds: All three strands verify from bytes. MT 20:3 opens verse-initially with “וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה”, and the amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census lists that verse among its MT keys — a tier-1 speech-frame signal under the evidence policy whatever weight it is finally given. The row nonetheless asserts flatly that ‘the bytes offer no internal tier-1 seam’ between command and interpretation, without quoting or answering that onset: the assertion is stated, not tested. The mislabel is byte-confirmed. MT 20:2 carries “בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ” followed IN THE SAME VERSE by the imperative run “לֵ֗ךְ וּפִתַּחְתָּ֤ הַשַּׂק֙” and the compliance clause “וַיַּ֣עַשׂ כֵּ֔ן” — that is the COMMAND frame; the interpretation of the sign-act (‘as my servant Isaiah has walked …’) opens at MT 20:3 under the divine-speech onset. Calling MT 20:2 the interpretive frame inverts the two, and the inversion sits in the row's load-bearing sentence. Both quoted runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against MT 20:2 and MT 20:3: the NFD class. Marks re-checked at MT keys: SAMEKH at MT 19:25, 20:2, 20:6, all correct and correctly typed; the mark at MT 20:2 is disclosed as mid-span but never set against the tier-1 onset it abuts, and the tier-3 layer is correctly not asked to drive anything. Credits confirmed: the servant handling is right — the my-servant form at MT 20:3 is a NAMED referent (the prophet), correctly kept apart from the unnamed servant-figure zones, and the row decides no referent question; the operative-category deviation from the report label toward continuous third-person narration is honestly disclosed rather than argued away. A split at 20:2|20:3 is a respan PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption and is not proposed here.

P05-010.challenge_claim: The sentence that defeats the row's own rival is falsified by the row's own quoted bytes — MT 21:6 carries a divine-speech frame with an explicit addressee, and the span's petuchah stands immediately before it; two in-span paseq segs go undisclosed and both pointed runs re-collate at NFD only.
P05-010.grounds: The core strand is decisive and self-inflicted. The row's rejected alternative says the banquet-to-commissioning transition 'is not marked by an addressee or frame-device shift in the bytes', two sentences after the row itself quotes “כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י” from MT 21:6. Both halves of that sentence fail. Frame-device: the divine-speech census lists MT 21:6 among the divine-frame sites and names it explicitly as a non-adjacent title form — a koh-amar frame unquestionably stands at the very transition called unmarked. Addressee: beyond the first-person dative “אֵלַ֖י” inside the formula, the surrounding bytes carry an actual shift — MT 21:5 addresses a plural group (“ק֥וּמוּ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים”) while MT 21:6 directs the speech to the prophet and commands him singly (“לֵ֚ךְ הַעֲמֵ֣ד”). The rival the row concedes is therefore left undefeated by the row's own quoted material. Corroboration re-checked at MT keys: the mark at MT 21:5 is a PE, correctly typed as the rarer type against the 41 PE / 168 SAMEKH inventory over 209 marked verses, with SAMEKH at MT 20:6 and MT 21:10 — all accurate, all correctly held at tier-3 single-witness and never as a driver, and it sits at the 21:5|21:6 junction. Paseq segs are recorded at MT 21:2 (2 segs) and MT 21:8 (1 seg) and neither is disclosed although both parashah marks in the span are — a real symmetry gap. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd against MT 21:1 and MT 21:6: the NFD class. Credits confirmed: the massa header at MT 21:1 is genuinely verse-initial; the frame ownership at MT 21:6 is correctly named as divine despite the intervening dative, which is the harder half to get right; the continuation-fold disclosure on the header verse is accurate in the staged layout and correctly held at tier-4. OL also observes that the same frame class is given seam force ten verses later; that is adjudicated on the row where it is charged. This ruling adjudicates the defective sentence only — the 21:1-10 watchman-vision construal is a known low-confidence hold and is NOT decided here.
P05-010.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the concession so it states what actually stands at MT 21:6 — a divine koh-amar frame carrying a first-person dative, with the address changing from MT 21:5's plural imperatives to a singular command to the prophet — and then gives the ground on which the vision is nonetheless held whole across it; test = no sentence in the row is contradicted by a run the row itself quotes, and the rival is answered rather than restated. (3) device_notes: disclose the paseq segs at MT 21:2 (2 segs) and MT 21:8 (1 seg), single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position; test = the span-relevant seg-disclosure symmetry sweep over 21:1-10 finds nothing undisclosed. (4) Because strongest_rejected_alternative is a driver-dependent field, re-open observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence alongside the re-cut and re-check each against the corrected warrant; test = the dependent fields are re-derived, not carried over. Any split at 21:5|21:6 is a respan PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption; the held construal stays held.

P05-011.challenge_claim: The bounds are byte-clean and survive challenge, but both pointed runs labelled byte tier re-collate at NFD only and the 'bracket' reading overstates an intra-verse doubling whose two members differ in the bytes; no byte-true device straddles either seam because the preceding unit's watch vocabulary is a different root.
P05-011.grounds: The two charged defects are real; the reviewer's own cross-seam clearance is not, and the corrected finding adds a third defect. (a) NFD confirmed: both pointed runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against MT 21:11. (b) The doubling confirmed: member A “שֹׁמֵר֙ מַה מִלַּ֔יְלָה” and member B “שֹׁמֵ֖ר מַה מִלֵּֽיל” fail identity at byte, at accent_stripped AND at skeleton — the night-forms differ (skeleton “מלילה” against “מליל”), so no tier makes the two members identical; only the watchman member itself repeats, and only at skeleton tier. The row's 'carries a repeated watchman question as its own bracket' is thus an untiered recurrence claim that is false as identity at every tier, and 'bracket' is the wrong figure besides: the repetition is immediate and intra-verse, not an inclusio around the two-verse unit, and the refrain-keyed substrate signal rides on that reading. (c) CORRECTED FINDING, new: OL clears cross-seam cohesion on the ground that the preceding unit's watch vocabulary is 'a DIFFERENT root — … and “כָּל” at MT 21:8'. That is byte-false at MT 21:8. “כָּל” is a shamar-root noun — its skeleton “כל” contains “שמר” contiguously — and the shamar skeleton stands at exactly MT 21:8, 21:11 and 21:12 in ch 21, so the root DOES straddle this row's opening seam. Only the watcher-noun at MT 21:6 and the lookout-noun at MT 21:8 are the genuinely different tsaphah root. The continuity is skeleton-tier and therefore weak, not the byte-true device the cohesion rule aims at, and the seam is not threatened — verse-initial massa headers stand at MT 21:11 and MT 21:13, tier-1, and the bounds hold — but the row owes the disclosure and the reviewer cleared it in error. Marks re-checked at MT keys: SAMEKH at MT 21:10 and MT 21:12, correct and correctly typed; no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls in 21:11-12, so nothing further is owed there. Severity stays low: no strand touches the boundary.
P05-011.remedy: Author work order, three edits, no boundary change. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'carries a repeated watchman question as its own bracket' with a tier-labelled description — an immediate intra-verse doubling whose watchman member repeats at skeleton tier while the night-forms differ at every tier — and re-check the refrain-keyed substrate signal against the corrected reading, demoting it if the corrected description no longer supports a refrain; test = every recurrence claim in the row names its tier and reproduces at that tier from the spliced bytes. (3) device_notes: disclose the shamar-root continuity across the row's opening seam (skeleton tier: MT 21:8 into MT 21:11-12) together with the tier-1 header warrant that survives it; test = the cross-seam cohesion sweep over both of the row's own seams finds nothing undisclosed, and the disclosure names its tier.

P05-012.challenge_claim: An undisclosed catchword hooks this row's closing verse to the next unit's at an oracle join, the mark prose places a setumah inside a span it does not fall in, the in-span paseq is dropped at the very verse whose setumah is cited, and the header run re-collates at NFD only.
P05-012.grounds: Three strands verify exactly; the fourth is overstated and its tier is under-named. (a) MARK POSITION, confirmed: the row's span is Isa.21.13-Isa.21.15 and its device_notes say 'a setumah opens this row at Isa.21.12'. The neighbouring row in the same part uses the correct form ('a setumah precedes this row at Isa.21.15'), so this is a local slip rather than a convention. (b) PASEQ, confirmed: a paseq seg is recorded at MT 21:15 (1 seg) and is undisclosed in the very verse the row cites for its setumah — one verse, two seg layers, one engaged and one dropped. (c) NFD, confirmed: the header run re-collates at nfd against MT 21:13; it is the row's only pointed run. (d) OVERSTATED and MIS-TIERED: the catchword is real but weaker than charged. “קֶ֣שֶׁת” at MT 21:15 and “קֶ֛שֶׁת” at MT 21:17 differ ONLY in accent, so they match at accent_stripped, not merely at skeleton as the challenge says — and nothing here is byte-true. It is an ordinary common noun (skeleton sweep: 8 verses book-wide, 3 verses in chs 20-23 — MT 21:15, 21:17, 22:3); it does not straddle the row's own seam directly, since it skips the seam verse MT 21:16; and both sites sit inside the same massa-header-bound Arabia material, where lexical continuity is expected rather than probative. Disclosure is still owed under the cross-seam cohesion rule, but the corrected finding is a weak accent_stripped-tier lexical hook, NOT 'the byte support' for the rival the row concedes. Credits confirmed: the massa header at MT 21:13 is genuinely verse-initial and correctly claimed. This ruling does not decide the Arabia-oracle construal, which is a known hold.

P05-013.challenge_claim: LF: the row treats a mid-oracle divine-frame formula as sufficient to open a fresh row while the neighbouring row in the same part treats the same device-class occurrence as carrying no cutting force, and the row does not reconcile the two even though its own rationale names the parallel. OL: the parallel is false at every tier — the two openings differ in token order — and it collapses the adjacent/non-adjacent title distinction on which the earlier site's classification rests.
P05-013.grounds: Both items land on one sentence — 'paralleling the identical frame construction opening the wilderness-of-the-sea vision report earlier in this part' — and they are DISTINCT defects, not one; the second does not dissolve the first. OL's is byte-decisive: MT 21:6 opens “כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י” and MT 21:16 opens “כִּי כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י” — the dative precedes the title at the first site and follows it at the second. The two fail identity at byte, at accent_stripped AND at skeleton (“כי כה אמר אלי אדני” against “כי כה אמר אדני אלי”). 'Identical frame construction' is therefore false at every available tier, and it additionally carries no tier label where campaign practice requires the tier named at write time. The distinction OL protects is load-bearing: the divine-speech census names MT 21:6 explicitly among the non-adjacent title forms whose divine ownership must be ARGUED rather than read off an adjacency, while MT 21:16 is the plain adjacent form that needs no such argument — flattening them erases the ground on which the earlier frame was owned. LF's is a warrant defect and SURVIVES OL's finding: the census lists both MT 21:6 and MT 21:16 under divine frames and neither under royal-messenger, so the two sites are one device CLASS even though they are not one form, and the row gives that class seam force here while the neighbouring row holds its own occurrence internal to an unbroken unit on the stated ground that no 'addressee or frame-device shift' marks it. Neither row reconciles the opposite weights, and this row's disclosed alternative addresses only whether to keep the Arabia oracle whole. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd against MT 21:16 and MT 21:17: the NFD class. The bare unpointed root mention beside the remnant quote is a skeleton-grade mention carrying no tier label. Marks re-checked at MT keys: SAMEKH at MT 21:15 and MT 21:17, correct and correctly typed. Credit confirmed: the remnant object is named correctly as the shear NOUN, kept apart from the Shear-Jashub name and from the reactivating clauses — exactly the four-way discipline this book demands. The defect is warrant quality, not boundary falsity: MT 21:16 does carry a divine koh-amar frame, and the preceding row is plain scene description.
P05-013.remedy: Author work order, three edits; WARRANT repair only. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both pointed runs from source bytes and tier-label the bare unpointed root mention as skeleton-grade; test = byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.21.16 and oshb:Isa.21.17, Hebrew-normalization dry-run clean, and no untiered Hebrew mention remains in the row. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'the identical frame construction' with the byte-true relation — the same divine koh-amar frame CLASS but not the same form: the two differ in token order and fail identity at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton, and MT 21:6 is the non-adjacent title form while MT 21:16 is the adjacent one; test = the corrected sentence reproduces from the two spliced runs at the tier it names AND preserves rather than erases the adjacency distinction on which the earlier site's divine ownership rests. (3) boundary_rationale or strongest_rejected_alternative: state the reconciliation — why this one device class carries seam force at MT 21:16 and none at MT 21:6 — or withdraw the parallel outright; test = the test that killed the original, namely that the same device class is not assigned opposite seam weights inside one part without a stated ground, checked against the neighbouring vision-report row's own warrant. Any consequent respan of either row is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption; the 21:1-10 and 21:13-17 construals are held and are not decided here.
